explanation: Collect each person in the bucket for their age, then copy the buckets back into the same list. Each age occupies one contiguous segment and every original (age,name) entry is preserved.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected time using hashing. Counting/bucketing scans n records; each write or slot-filling swap permanently places one record. Hash operations are expected constant time.
spaceComplexity: O(n) auxiliary space. Bucket variants retain n records; offset/count variants retain one map entry per distinct age.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Every person is copied into exactly one bucket keyed by their age. Writing complete buckets back preserves the multiset of people and gives each age one contiguous output segment. The contract leaves group order unrestricted.
walkthrough: For [(6,"Nyx"),(2,"Bo"),(6,"Ana")], the age-6 bucket holds Nyx and Ana and the age-2 bucket holds Bo. One produced ordering is [(6,"Nyx"),(6,"Ana"),(2,"Bo")]; every person remains and equal ages are contiguous.
edgeCases: Repeated names still represent separate people and must be preserved.
A single age already forms a valid group.
Group order is unrestricted, so compare structure and membership rather than one fixed sorted order.
